content: 1. Dinoprostone is a medication used to prepare the cervix (the lower opening of the uterus) for labor and delivery. It is typically administered to women who are at or near their delivery due date and are experiencing a normal pregnancy. 2. Dinoprostone is a naturally occurring substance in the body that plays a role in preparing for labor. 3. This medication is inserted high into the vagina, near the cervix, by a healthcare professional. During the procedure, the patient will lie down, and it is usually necessary to remain lying down for two hours after the insertion. 4. Dinoprostone should only be used in a hospital setting where trained medical professionals are available to provide care. 5. Patients will be closely monitored for changes in the cervix, signs of active labor (such as the breaking of water or strong, sustained contractions), and the condition of the baby. 6. The healthcare professional will remove the insert if side effects occur, after 12 hours, or when it is no longer needed. 7. Common side effects of dinoprostone include fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. These effects are generally mild and uncommon. 8. Rarely, this medication can cause uterine rupture, a serious condition that may require emergency surgery. Symptoms of uterine rupture include severe pain in the uterus and an abnormal heart rate in the baby. 9. Serious allergic reactions to dinoprostone are rare but can occur. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may include difficulty breathing, swelling, or rash. 10. Dinoprostone should be used with caution in patients with epilepsy, glaucoma, liver or kidney impairment, or pulmonary disease. 11. Patients with a history of cardiovascular disorders, such as myocardial infarction, should be closely monitored during treatment. 12. Dinoprostone may increase the effects of oxytocin due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Therefore, caution and close monitoring are advised when these medications are used together. 13. After removing a dinoprostone insert, wait at least 30 minutes before administering other oxytocic drugs. If a gel form of dinoprostone was used, wait 6-12 hours before administering other oxytocic drugs. 14. The gel form of dinoprostone should not be applied above the level of the internal cervical os. 15. Patients with conditions such as cervical laceration, acute vaginitis, anemia, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypotension, or uterine fibroids should be monitored closely during treatment. 16. Women aged 30 years or older, those with pregnancy complications, or those with a gestational age greater than 40 weeks may have an increased risk of postpartum disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). These patients should be assessed for evolving fibrinolysis in the immediate postpartum period, and appropriate therapy should be promptly initiated if needed. 17. In rare cases, disruption and embolization of antigenic tissue may lead to the development of an anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy. 18. Life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported. These reactions can occur within minutes to hours after starting therapy. If a hypersensitivity reaction is suspected, discontinue dinoprostone therapy immediately, assess for other potential causes, and provide symptomatic and supportive treatment as needed. 19. Dinoprostone is indicated for the initiation or continuation of cervical ripening in pregnant women at or near term who have a medical or obstetrical indication for labor induction. 20. Limited data on the use of dinoprostone in pregnant women do not show a clear association with adverse developmental outcomes. Relevant animal reproduction data for dinoprostone are not available. 21. If therapy is discontinued due to fetal distress, a return to normal fetal heart rhythm has been observed, with no neonatal sequelae. Therapy should be removed in cases of persistent tachysystole, with or without changes in fetal heart rate, and institutional protocols for patient management should be followed. 22. Dinoprostone is not indicated for use in breastfeeding women, as there is no information on its effects on breastfed children or milk production. 23. Before using dinoprostone, inform your doctor, midwife, or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 24. During pregnancy, dinoprostone should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. 25. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of dinoprostone or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all medications and products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 26. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. If someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. 27. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused products. 28. This information is not exhaustive and does not replace the advice of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
